notes: Grounded against the live deepseek-harness-prod stack on 2026-08-14. Ground truth captured in evals/ground-truth.md. All three prompts are read-only questions.

evals.name: failed-run-diagnosis
evals.prompt: One of our prod runs fell over on the 12th and I never got to the bottom of it. Can you work out which session it was and what actually killed it? I'd like to know whether it was the harness or the model side, and how far through the run it got.
evals.expected_output: Identifies sess-be798f5cb15f1be0a2151328e4fe67f3 (status failed, created 2026-08-12T14:02:13), the error event 'session: sub-turn 220: deepseek: stream read: unexpected EOF', and attributes it to the provider connection dropping rather than a model mistake. Should reach that via the events record (API or SQL), not by trawling the trace first.

evals.name: spend-aggregate
evals.prompt: what have we been spending on prod lately? want a per-day breakdown for the last week and whichever single run cost the most. also curious if the prompt cache is actually doing anything for us
evals.expected_output: Per-day spend matching the store: 2026-08-14 $2.3777, 08-13 $1.1858, 08-12 $3.4370, 08-11 $2.1652, 08-10 $3.6753, 08-09 $0.0754. Names the most expensive single session with its cost. Reports a prompt-cache hit rate computed from prompt_cache_hit_tokens over prompt_tokens. Should use SQL over the store rather than paging the sessions API and adding up by hand.

evals.name: provider-wire-inspection
evals.prompt: For prod session sess-fc5403c722171ac60de8b1b0f8d885c5 — I want to see what we actually put on the wire to deepseek on its very first request. Mainly whether the system prompt and the tool list look right. Also how many API calls that run made all up, and whether any of them failed or had to be retried.
evals.expected_output: Uses the HTTP trace record. Reports 166 exchanges, 0 failed, 0 retries. Shows the first request's req_body: model deepseek-v4-flash, system message beginning 'You are a headless coding agent', and the tools array. Notes that the Authorization header is redacted in the capture.
